items.description: No run-to-run variance, confidence intervals, or significance tests accompany any of the comparative nDCG@10 numbers in Tables 2, 3, 4, 9 or 10 (or the derived 'Avg. Performance vs. BM25' percentages). The authors state this is because most evaluated systems are public pre-trained checkpoints without accessible training code, so re-training for repeated seeds was not feasible in many cases.
items.resolution_status: author-explained, not resolvable from this project folder
items.action_taken: Reported as an author-stated limitation (L006); all comparative claims in the draft describe point estimates only and avoid language implying statistical significance.

items.description: Four of the 19 datasets used or referenced (BioASQ, Signal-1M(RT), TREC-NEWS, Robust04) are not directly downloadable from the project's own distribution (README marks them 'Public? = No', with a 'How to Reproduce?' pointer instead of a direct link).
items.resolution_status: author-documented access constraint, not a defect in the reported results
items.action_taken: Not surfaced as a limitation of the reported findings (it bears on reproducibility/access, not on the validity of the numbers already reported); noted here for completeness.

items.description: The paper reports the GPU/CPU hardware used for the latency benchmark (Table 3) but explicitly does not report total compute used across the whole study (NeurIPS checklist item 4d).
items.action_taken: Not elevated to a formal limitation in the claim map, since no claim in the draft depends on total compute; mentioned only if space allows in Methods.

items.description: The TREC-COVID annotation-bias case study (Table 4) was run on one dataset only; whether the same lexical annotation-pool bias, and at what magnitude, applies to the other 17 BEIR datasets is not tested anywhere in the evidence.
items.resolution_status: acknowledged scope boundary; addressed as a writer-derived limitation (L008), since the authors themselves generalize cautiously ('Better datasets... are needed for a fair evaluation') without claiming the magnitude found on TREC-COVID applies elsewhere.
